subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Warrant Canaries
description: A quick, practical guide to Warrant Canaries.

hook.text: A company can't tell you the government demanded your data. So it tells you by saying nothing at all.

buildup.text: A warrant canary is a public statement saying: 'We have NOT received any secret government data demands.'

discovery.text: If the statement disappears, users know a secret order was received — without the company saying a word.

twist.text: The legal status of warrant canaries is untested. Governments could argue that removing one violates the gag order.

climax.text: Companies use creative silence to fight government secrecy. It's a legal gray area born from desperation.

punchline.text: Can't speak? Let your silence do the talking.

quiz.question: How does a warrant canary work?
options: Its removal signals that a secret government data demand has been received
It encrypts all user data automatically
It blocks government access to servers
